mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: In high-interest-rate regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate future easing and demand for equities rises.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when the CPIAUCSL decline trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in a month coincides with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports optimism about corporate earnings.
failure_condition: In periods of labor market expansion, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS crosses the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and retail sales (HOUST) by at least 2% in the same month signals weakening overall economic demand, which predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change <= -2% AND HOUST monthly change <= -2%
failure_condition: During periods of dual demand weakness, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% for three consecutive months suggests improving supply conditions, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: In supply-recovery regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite sustained INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3.5% (implied by UNRATE < 3.5), the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased consumer confidence and investment optimism.
failure_condition: In low-unemployment regimes, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail activity (HOUST) of more than 4% in a month combined with a decline in consumer spending proxies (not available in this catalog) would typically drive a negative S&P 20-day forward return. However, using only observable proxies, a simultaneous drop in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST by >4% predicts a negative return over 20 days due to pessimism about demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change <= -4% AND RSAFS monthly change <= -4%
failure_condition: During retail contraction, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both proxies fall by >4%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month while the federal funds rate remains unchanged, the S&P 60-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to recessionary risk and reduced equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly change > 0.2 and FEDFUNDS previous month <= FEDFUNDS current month
failure_condition: In this regime, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite the trigger.
